title: Apple Unseats Nvidia as World's Most Valuable Company as AI Spending Fears Mount

body:
Key Takeaways
  • Apple's market cap reached $4.89 trillion, surpassing Nvidia's $4.85 trillion.
  • Nvidia's AI spending concerns are growing, impacting its revenue growth potential.
  • Apple's AI spending is only 2.5% of estimated sales, compared to 39% for hyperscalers.
  • Apple shares rose nearly 15% this quarter, while the Nasdaq fell 1.1%.
  • India's tech ecosystem is affected by the Apple-Nvidia rivalry, impacting local AI startups.

Apple briefly reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company on Friday, with its market capitalisation touching $4.89 trillion — narrowly edging out Nvidia's $4.85 trillion. It is the first time in over a year that the chipmaker has been dethroned from the top spot, and the shuffle signals a meaningful shift in how Wall Street is pricing the artificial intelligence trade.

The 'Anti-AI' Trade

For much of the past two years, Nvidia has been the undisputed king of the AI boom, becoming the primary hardware supplier for the massive infrastructure buildout by hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta. The company became the first to hit a $5 trillion valuation late last year.

But growing unease about the sustainability of AI capital expenditure is catching up. In recent months, soaring financial commitments from tech giants — despite limited returns from their AI investments — have alarmed analysts, with some painting doomsday scenarios of these companies' cash flows turning negative. If that happens, Nvidia's revenue growth could peak as well.

Apple, by contrast, has been characterised as the "anti-AI" trade. The Cupertino giant has kept its AI spending to roughly 2.5 percent of estimated sales, compared with 39 percent for the hyperscalers, according to HSBC analyst Nicolas Cote-Colisson, who upgraded Apple to "buy" on Friday with a $366 price target.

The Rockefeller Playbook

Barron's likened Apple's strategy to John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil playbook: letting wildcatters bear the risky drilling costs while controlling the distribution end. Apple is letting its Magnificent Seven peers spend heavily on AI research and development, ready to adopt the best models once the dust settles — while monetising AI through services, ecosystem lock-in, and hardware upgrades.

The strategy appears to be working. Apple shares are up nearly 15 percent this quarter, while the Nasdaq is down 1.1 percent. The stock hit record highs for two consecutive days this week after the public beta release of iOS 27 showcased a redesigned, LLM-powered Siri.

Indian Tech at the Crossroads

The Apple-Nvidia rivalry matters deeply to India's technology ecosystem. Indian engineers occupy senior roles at both companies — from chip design teams in Cupertino and Santa Clara to AI research labs. Apple's expanded $30 billion chip supply deal with Broadcom and its pursuit of AI server chip startups could create ripple effects in India's semiconductor ambitions, particularly as the country pushes its own chip fabrication agenda.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's dominance has fuelled a boom in AI startups across Bengaluru and Hyderabad, many of which rely on its GPUs. Any slowdown in Nvidia's growth trajectory could temper venture capital enthusiasm for Indian AI companies.

A fresh catalyst from China also weighed on Nvidia. Chinese AI startup Moonshot debuted its Kimi K3 model on Thursday — a 2.8 trillion-parameter model that matched frontier American models at lower cost, echoing the DeepSeek R1 moment from early 2025 that briefly knocked Nvidia off its perch.

"Apple is less exposed to capex intensity and better positioned to monetise AI via services, ecosystem lock-in, and hardware upgrades," Toni Meadows, head of investment at BRI Wealth Management, told Reuters. For now, the market seems to agree.
